title: A loop needs a way out

chalkboard.title: Why does this loop never stop?

steps.say: We call halve_until_one(8). It should count how many halvings take 8 down to 1: three.
Is 8 > 1? Yes, so we enter the loop.
Back to the test: is 8 > 1? Still yes. Nothing in the body changed n.
steps.error_label: Bug: the loop never changes n, so the test is always True and the loop never ends.

steps.say: Fix: add n = n // 2 in the body. Then n goes 8, 4, 2, 1 and the loop stops after 3 passes.

pages.title: A loop needs a way out
paragraphs: A while loop checks its condition before every pass and stops as soon as the condition is False.
Something inside the body has to move the loop toward that exit. If nothing the condition depends on ever changes, the loop runs forever.

key_term.definition: the test checked before every pass; the loop stops when it is False.

pages.title: Check the bounds first
paragraphs: When a loop reads items by index, the index has to stay inside the list. Reading nums[i] after i has passed the end raises IndexError.
Python reads 'and' from left to right and stops at the first False. Put i < len(nums) first, so nums[i] is only read when i is valid.

key_term.definition: 'and' stops at the first False, so the right side is never evaluated.

transcript: A while loop asks its question before every single pass.
The moment the answer is False, the loop stops.
So something inside the loop has to change what the question depends on.
If nothing changes, the answer stays True and the loop never ends.
When the loop walks through a list, check the index is in range before you read the item.
With and, Python stops at the first False, so put the bounds check first.
